steps:
Create ONE cutout torso piece for the ACROBAT character of a 2D Godot game, matching EXACTLY the art style of the attached head sheet (hand-inked 1930s rubber-hose cartoon, thick dark brown outline #1b1410, subtle painted shading).

View: three-quarter view facing RIGHT, the SAME angle as the attached head, so the head can sit on top of it naturally.

Content, top to bottom:
- A short slim NECK rising from the chest (the top of the neck will be hidden behind the head).
- Narrow, gently sloping shoulders, both small; the far shoulder mostly hidden behind the body. NO arms at all (arms are drawn separately as thin rubber-hose tubes coming out of the shoulders).
- Teal (#1f5a66) strapless-style leotard with gold trim, thin gold shoulder straps, sweetheart neckline, a gold star at the waist, slim waist.
- Bottom: the leotard ends at the hips with the gold zigzag hem. NO legs (legs are drawn separately).

Proportions: slim, small torso, about 1.3x taller than wide. Single isolated piece, centered, fully TRANSPARENT background, no shadow, no text, no grid, about 1024 px tall.

Reference clarification: the attached sheet is a STYLE AND HEAD-ANGLE reference only. Use the acrobat HEAD in the TOP LEFT cell to match the right-facing three-quarter perspective, warm skin tone, organic ink weight, and painted shading. Ignore all other components of that sheet, especially its torso. Output ONLY the new torso described above; do not include the head or another sheet.
Critical silhouette: slim neck, delicate sloping shoulders without round bulbous shoulder caps, no arm stubs or sockets sticking outward; far shoulder is a small mostly occluded edge. Torso naturally oriented toward the right, not a broad symmetric front-facing bust. No thighs, bare leg stubs, feet, hands, gloves or head. End the complete ink-outlined piece at the gold-trimmed hip/crotch hem. Keep the entire piece visible with small clear transparent margins. Genuine alpha transparency.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the torso EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is the HEAD STYLE AND PERSPECTIVE reference only. Output ONE isolated torso, not a sheet.

Correct the silhouette of image 1 to make it a valid CUTOUT TORSO for the rubber-hose acrobat. Keep its teal #1f5a66 and gold costume, waist star, painted texture, warm skin color and thick dark brown #1b1410 hand-inked outlines matching the head in image 2, and preserve the three-quarter view facing RIGHT.

REQUIRED CUTOUT CORRECTIONS:
1. Completely REMOVE both pale skin THIGH STUBS below the gold zigzag hem. Those skin areas must become TRANSPARENT. The whole bottom silhouette is ONLY the ink-outlined teal leotard and its gold zigzag trim, down to the intact pointed crotch. No skin below or inside the lower hip openings. No legs or leg fragments.
2. REMOVE the large rounded BULBOUS left shoulder cap/upper-arm stump. Replace it with a SMALL NARROW GENTLY SLOPING shoulder edge seamlessly joining the upper chest. The far shoulder at right is mostly hidden behind the body, just a small sloped edge. There are ZERO arms, zero bicep shapes, no sockets and no circular shoulder lobes.
3. Keep a short slim neck stub extending upward from the chest, positioned to fit the supplied head. The neck is a narrow trapezoid, not long.
4. Remove the two gold chest buttons; retain the thin gold shoulder straps, sweetheart gold neckline, and ONE gold star at the waist. Make the costume front a modest smooth cartoon bodice, without strongly separated oversized circular bust cups.
5. Make the torso SLIM and COMPACT, around 1.3 times taller than wide, measured including neck to the leotard tip. Natural small shoulders, slim waist, gently flared hips. Same three-quarter RIGHT-facing angle as image 2, with the far chest/shoulder narrower from perspective.

Canvas/output: one complete centered component, true transparent alpha background, approximately 1024 pixels tall with small clear transparent margins. No head, hair, earring, arms, hands, thighs, legs, feet, grid, labels, shadow, text or watermark. Hand-painted 1930s cartoon cutout, not an icon. Preserve the style and costume details while correcting only this torso component's silhouette.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the torso EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is the matching HEAD reference.
Make ONE targeted change: correct the torso's PROPORTIONS and upper shoulder/neck contour while retaining its painted art, costume colors, gold trim, gold waist star, right-facing three-quarter perspective and absence of arms/legs.

The current torso is much too elongated. Redraw it as a COMPACT small torso about 1.3 times TALLER than its maximum width. Enforce this: the visible silhouette from neck top to leotard crotch tip must be approximately 780 pixels TALL by 600 pixels WIDE, centered on a SQUARE 1024 x 1024 transparent canvas. This is NOT a tall 1.8:1 torso. Use the same scale for neck/shoulders/body, with a SHORT SLIM neck stub no more than 65 pixels tall, rising at the top center-right to fit the supplied head.

Restore a tiny natural gently SLOPING near shoulder edge at the top left, smoothly connecting to the chest and thin gold strap. It should not be a bulbous arm cap, and not a large deep circular arm socket. Far shoulder on the right is just a small sloped mostly hidden edge. No arm stubs, arms or hands.
Compress the bare upper chest and midriff to natural short cartoon proportions. Slightly slim, softly shaded sweetheart bodice; do not enlarge round bust shapes. Gold waist star, slim waist, gently flared gold zigzag hip hem. Bottom is only teal fabric and gold trim down to a complete pointed crotch silhouette, with TRANSPARENT hip openings. No skin thighs or leg stubs anywhere under the hem.

Match head image 2 EXACTLY in 1930s hand-inked cartoon style, #1b1410 dark brown contours, warm skin, subtle painted shading. Teal fabric #1f5a66, gold trim and thin gold shoulder straps. Only torso including short neck, no head, hair, arms, hands, legs, feet, text, grid, watermark or cast shadow. Real alpha transparency. Keep the whole piece visible. Output a square canvas with the compact 780-high by 600-wide silhouette, not another portrait elongated image.

Edit this SINGLE transparent acrobat torso with ONE LOCAL CHANGE: make the NECK AND BARE UPPER CHEST MUCH SHORTER.

Keep everything BELOW the golden sweetheart neckline exactly as drawn: the teal leotard, slim waist, gold waist star, zigzag gold hip/crotch hem, texture, right-facing perspective, dark brown outline, no legs. Preserve the current tiny shoulder edges and open side arm attachment cut, no arms.

The region ABOVE the gold sweetheart neckline has too much vertical height. Compress ONLY that neck-and-upper-chest region to HALF of its present height, with a SHORT slim neck stub and delicate sloping shoulders. Keep its WIDTH the same. Smoothly redraw the ink contours, straps and collarbone shading to connect naturally. In particular, cut the vertical neck length by 50%, and cut the bare chest distance from shoulder line to sweetheart neckline by 50%.

This should make the complete visible torso, neck top to leotard crotch tip, about 1.3 times TALLER than WIDE. Do NOT stretch the whole torso or enlarge its chest. Do NOT add rounded shoulder caps, arms, skin thighs or legs. Only reduce the excessive vertical extent of the upper bare region. One isolated complete piece, center it with transparent margins, about 1024 px high canvas, alpha transparency. No head, limbs, text, grid, watermark, shadow or other changes. Keep the hand-inked 1930s painted cartoon art and #1b1410 outline.
preparation: Godot: crop transparent margins and resize proportionally to 976px foreground height on a transparent 1024px-high canvas. No runtime scene or script modified.
